source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 15: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and scope: the launcher, backend and versions, world size, hosts, scheduler, container permissions, network fabric/interfaces, GPU topology, and exact hang stage are unknown. Treat these as hypotheses to measure, not facts. This is scenario variant 15.

Diagnosis and containment:
1. Capture job/run ID, host, rank/local-rank/world-size, PID, timestamps, initialization stage, backend/transport versions, launch environment, stderr, and store/rendezvous endpoint (redacting secrets). Confirm exactly one process per expected rank, identical world/rank membership, matching rendezvous endpoint, and identical collective/barrier ordering. Bound the watchdog/timeout and terminate only the isolated diagnostic job; preserve logs and clean up processes before retrying.
2. Check GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping, device count, driver/runtime compatibility, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, clocks, container device permissions, ulimits, shared-memory and socket resources. Test the selected interface explicitly (address, route, DNS, MTU/firewall and reachability) and compare with an alternate permitted interface without changing unrelated variables.
3. Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous or transport path fails, so one or more ranks never enter the same collective. Support requires a consistent missing/late rank or interface error and recovery when the endpoint/interface or rank membership is corrected. Falsify it if every rank reaches the same barrier, a minimal same-node all-reduce passes, and repeated full-world hangs persist with rendezvous/interface telemetry clean; then investigate topology, algorithm, tensor-size, driver, or resource causes.
4. Run a randomized, blocked experiment matrix using the same image/configuration and allocated hosts: (a) single-node minimal all-reduce, (b) reduced world crossing each suspect host/link, and (c) full world. Keep world size, tensor dtype/size, timeout, interface, and topology fixed within blocks; then vary one factor at a time (interface, transport/algorithm, tensor size, host pair, or rank mapping). Record per-rank entry/exit timestamps, store connection events, selected NIC/path, retransmits/errors, GPU/NCCL telemetry, CPU/memory, and timeout/cleanup outcomes. Repeat enough times for denominators, not just a successful trial.
5. Compare outcomes by rank and block: success, initialization timeout, hang, rank crash, transport error, and cleanup failure. Require correctness (all-reduce checksum), bounded initialization latency, and no leaked processes before accepting a mitigation. Do not label a cause from correlation alone; distinguish rank membership, endpoint, interface/MTU/firewall, topology/peer access, software mismatch, resource exhaustion, and scheduler/host instability as competing explanations.

Rollback and evidence: keep the last known-good launch configuration; canary any interface, transport, timeout, topology, or rank-mapping change on an isolated job, with an explicit abort threshold for hangs/errors/latency regressions and automatic return to the known-good configuration. Evidence required: complete per-rank logs and rendezvous membership, exact versions/configuration, topology and GPU mapping, interface/path diagnostics, minimal/reduced/full matrix results with repetitions and denominators, checksum/latency results, and cleanup logs. Confidence is provisional: without those measurements, no platform-specific root cause is established.
risks: Root cause remains unconfirmed without per-rank and transport telemetry.
Diagnostic retries can create orphaned processes or contaminate results if cleanup is incomplete.
Changing interface, topology, or timeout can mask an intermittent fault or trade hangs for silent correctness/latency regressions.
evidence_required: Per-rank rendezvous and collective-entry timestamps and logs
Exact software, launch, topology, GPU mapping, and interface configuration
Repeated randomized single-node/reduced-world/full-world results with outcome denominators
All-reduce checksum, initialization latency, timeout, and cleanup results

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 23: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and scope: the launcher, backend and versions, world size, hosts, scheduler, container permissions, network fabric/interfaces, GPU topology, and exact hang stage are unknown. Treat these as hypotheses to measure, not facts. This is scenario variant 23.

Diagnosis and containment:
1. Capture job/run ID, host, rank/local-rank/world-size, PID, timestamps, initialization stage, backend/transport versions, launch environment, stderr, and store/rendezvous endpoint (redacting secrets). Confirm exactly one process per expected rank, identical world/rank membership, matching rendezvous endpoint, and identical collective/barrier ordering. Bound the watchdog/timeout and terminate only the isolated diagnostic job; preserve logs and clean up processes before retrying.
2. Check GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping, device count, driver/runtime compatibility, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, clocks, container device permissions, ulimits, shared-memory and socket resources. Test the selected interface explicitly (address, route, DNS, MTU/firewall and reachability) and compare with an alternate permitted interface without changing unrelated variables.
3. Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous or transport path fails, so one or more ranks never enter the same collective. Support requires a consistent missing/late rank or interface error and recovery when the endpoint/interface or rank membership is corrected. Falsify it if every rank reaches the same barrier, a minimal same-node all-reduce passes, and repeated full-world hangs persist with rendezvous/interface telemetry clean; then investigate topology, algorithm, tensor-size, driver, or resource causes.
4. Run a randomized, blocked experiment matrix using the same image/configuration and allocated hosts: (a) single-node minimal all-reduce, (b) reduced world crossing each suspect host/link, and (c) full world. Keep world size, tensor dtype/size, timeout, interface, and topology fixed within blocks; then vary one factor at a time (interface, transport/algorithm, tensor size, host pair, or rank mapping). Record per-rank entry/exit timestamps, store connection events, selected NIC/path, retransmits/errors, GPU/NCCL telemetry, CPU/memory, and timeout/cleanup outcomes. Repeat enough times for denominators, not just a successful trial.
5. Compare outcomes by rank and block: success, initialization timeout, hang, rank crash, transport error, and cleanup failure. Require correctness (all-reduce checksum), bounded initialization latency, and no leaked processes before accepting a mitigation. Do not label a cause from correlation alone; distinguish rank membership, endpoint, interface/MTU/firewall, topology/peer access, software mismatch, resource exhaustion, and scheduler/host instability as competing explanations.

Rollback and evidence: keep the last known-good launch configuration; canary any interface, transport, timeout, topology, or rank-mapping change on an isolated job, with an explicit abort threshold for hangs/errors/latency regressions and automatic return to the known-good configuration. Evidence required: complete per-rank logs and rendezvous membership, exact versions/configuration, topology and GPU mapping, interface/path diagnostics, minimal/reduced/full matrix results with repetitions and denominators, checksum/latency results, and cleanup logs. Confidence is provisional: without those measurements, no platform-specific root cause is established.
